news.title: AI agents are quietly generating chaos engineering failures enterprises don’t track yet
news.summary_raw: There is a category of production incident that engineering teams are not tracking yet — because it doesn't fit any existing postmortem template. The agent initiated an action. The action was technically correct given the agent's context. The context was incomplete. The infrastructure cascaded. And, by the time the incident review happened, three teams were arguing about whether it was an agent failure or an infrastructure failure,  because the frameworks for thinking about these two t
news.summary: Production incidents caused by AI agents are not being tracked due to a lack of frameworks for understanding these failures. This has led to disputes between teams as to whether these incidents were caused by agents or infrastructure.
news.enterprise_use: Review your organization's incident tracking frameworks to ensure they account for AI agent failures and do not misattribute these to infrastructure issues. Check your logging and monitoring tools for any signs of AI agent activity that may be leading to unintended cascading failures. Consider using tools or platforms that can help identify and isolate AI agent activity, such as monitoring and logging tools that can provide granular visibility into agent activity.

news.title: Why prompt debt, retrieval debt, and evaluation debt are quietly reshaping enterprise AI risk
news.summary_raw: Over the past two decades, technical debt meant outdated architecture, messy code, and poorly maintained documentation. That definition is no longer sufficient in the AI era, where failure modes are more subtle and often non-linear. AI systems are introducing new layers of technical debt that live across prompts, models, and data dependencies — making these layers less visible, harder to measure, and often more dangerous than traditional debt.A crisis hiding in plain sightThe complexities of AI
news.summary: Experts discuss the growing issue of prompt debt, retrieval debt, and evaluation debt in AI systems, making them harder to measure and more dangerous. These new forms of technical debt pose substantial risks to enterprise AI adoption and deployment.
news.enterprise_use: While this is a general discussion, IT engineers should take note of the growing risk landscape and consider evaluating their AI system's dependencies and prompt engineering to mitigate potential issues.
